briefing.text: The tables appear to be an MSK-IMPACT HER2-positive esophagogastric cohort with trastuzumab outcome fields (e.g. HER2_RESPONSE, HER2_TTP_ON_1ST_LINE_MONTHS, HER2_TX_STATUS), a pre/post-treatment sample flag (IMPACT_PRE_POST) and ERBB2 status fields (HER2_IMPACT, HER2_IMPACT_LR, IHC_HER2, HER2_FISH). Confirm these columns exist. The absence of an explicit 'subclone' or clonality variable does not by itself put the claim out of scope; a usable proxy for selection of an ERBB2-non-amplified subclone is loss of ERBB2 amplification in post-trastuzumab samples relative to pre-treatment samples.
briefing.reason: Prevents scoping the hypothesis as out-of-study solely because no clonality column exists, and names the proxy variables to test.

briefing.text: Identify patients with both a PRE-TX and a POST-TX sample (multiple SAMPLE_IDs per PATIENT_ID) and tabulate ERBB2 status per patient across time points, checking that the post sample followed trastuzumab (TREATMENT / first-line comment fields). Base conclusions primarily on within-patient paired changes (ERBB2 amplified pre -> not amplified post); unpaired PRE vs POST group comparisons confound patient selection with acquired change and should be secondary.
briefing.reason: Defines the correct unit of analysis for an 'acquired' change.

briefing.text: ERBB2 amplification calls from panel sequencing depend on tumor purity, and the discrete CNA value (2 = amplification) can miss sub-threshold focal gains. For any sample switching from amplified to non-amplified, check the continuous ERBB2 log-ratio (segment mean over chr17 ~39.68-39.73 Mb hg19 in data_cna_hg19.seg, and HER2_IMPACT_LR) and the fraction genome altered; a flat, near-zero-FGA profile suggests low purity rather than true loss, while loss with other CNAs preserved supports a real change. Report discrete and continuous measures and flag uncertain cases.
briefing.reason: Distinguishes true ERBB2 loss from purity/threshold artefacts, which would otherwise bias the core measurement.

briefing.text: The number of paired post-trastuzumab samples is likely small, so tests have low power; a non-significant p-value is not evidence of no association. Report counts, the fraction of paired cases with ERBB2 loss, an exact test/CI, and weigh effect size together with established biology when the data alone are underpowered.
briefing.reason: Guards against reading 'no association' from an underpowered test.

briefing.text: Discordance between IHC/FISH HER2 (often from an earlier specimen) and sequencing-based HER2_IMPACT may reflect intratumoral HER2 heterogeneity, which is common in gastric cancer, not just assay error. A secondary analysis: cross-tab IHC_HER2/HER2_FISH vs HER2_IMPACT and relate pre-treatment ERBB2 non-amplification (heterogeneity proxy) to HER2_RESPONSE and HER2_TTP_ON_1ST_LINE_MONTHS.
briefing.reason: Gives an additional, complementary angle on non-amplified subpopulations and trastuzumab outcome.

briefing.text: Other resistance mechanisms (MET, EGFR, KRAS, PIK3CA, CCNE1 alterations) may co-occur in post-trastuzumab samples. Tabulate them alongside ERBB2 loss; the existence of other mechanisms does not negate an association of ERBB2 loss with resistance in the subset where it occurs.
briefing.reason: Prevents dismissing ERBB2 loss because it is not the only resistance mechanism observed.

shared_assumptions: Both teams equate 'selection for an ERBB2-non-amplified subclone' with a sample-level switch from AMP to non-AMP between a PRE-TX and a POST-TX biopsy, without testing whether the two biopsies came from the same site (primary vs metastasis), so spatial heterogeneity could look like temporal selection.

Both assume a POST-TX sample was taken at acquired resistance (progression on trastuzumab) rather than at any later time after treatment; neither tied the loss cases to the per-sample HER2_RESPONSE / HER2_TTP_ON_1ST_LINE_MONTHS or to patient-level treatment lines.

Both read the hypothesis's 'not associated' as refuted by the existence of a few loss events, rather than by a comparison of loss frequency in resistant vs non-resistant (or treated vs untreated) patients.
unused_evidence: SITE_OF_TISSUE_BIOPSY and SAMPLE_TYPE (Primary/Metastasis) for the paired samples: whether the 2 loss cases compare the same lesion or different sites.

HER2_RESPONSE, HER2_TTP_ON_1ST_LINE_MONTHS, HER2_TX_STATUS, DETAILS_FIRST_LINE_COMMENTS and NUMBER_OF_LINES for the loss patients vs the retained-amplification patients (was the loss sample at progression?).

data_mutations.txt and data_sv.txt: whether the post-treatment non-amplified sample shares truncal mutations with the pre-treatment sample (same tumor lineage, supporting subclone selection vs a different tumor/contamination).

data_cna_hg19.seg segment-level ERBB2 profiles and pre-treatment HER2 heterogeneity (IHC 2+ / FISH ratio vs IMPACT AMP discordance) related to response, which is a second route to a 'non-amplified subclone' reading.
unresolved_weak_points: Team A: only 2 loss events and no clonality variable; IHC/FISH and co-mechanism checks were named but not run.
Team B: only 2 loss events and 'no per-sample link to progression' — reported, not resolved; team B ran no pitfall checks (empty list), including no purity check on the loss samples.
Both rest the label partly on recollection of the source study's interpretation rather than on the data.
second_readings: 'Acquired trastuzumab resistance' could be read strictly as progression after initial response, so the relevant group is responders who later progressed, not all post-trastuzumab samples.

'Selection for a subclone' could be read as pre-existing heterogeneity (non-amplified cells present before treatment) that expands, which would be tested by pre-treatment HER2 heterogeneity vs outcome rather than by post-treatment loss alone.
challenge.verdict: Moderately high trust: both teams found direct paired evidence (2 AMP->non-AMP switches after trastuzumab) consistent with the study design, and the label convention favours the study's own finding. The main untested risks are that the switches reflect site or purity differences rather than selection, and that neither team linked them to documented progression.

questions.question: QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: For the 2 loss patients and the ~23 retained-amplification paired patients, tabulate SITE_OF_TISSUE_BIOPSY and SAMPLE_TYPE of each PRE-TX and POST-TX sample. Are the loss cases same-site comparisons or primary-vs-metastasis comparisons, and does that change whether you read them as temporal selection rather than spatial heterogeneity?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: Check whether the POST-TX non-amplified samples share the PRE-TX sample's truncal mutations (data_mutations.txt) and other arm-level CNAs (seg file). Does the overlap support the same tumor lineage, and does a low overlap change how you weigh the P-0000444 case?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: You named the IHC/FISH discordance check but did not run it. Cross-tabulate pre-treatment IHC_HER2/HER2_FISH vs HER2_IMPACT and compare HER2_RESPONSE and HER2_TTP_ON_1ST_LINE_MONTHS between concordant and discordant patients. Does this second line of evidence agree with or cut against your paired result?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: You say progression is not recorded per sample. For the two loss patients, read HER2_RESPONSE, HER2_TTP_ON_1ST_LINE_MONTHS, HER2_TX_STATUS and DETAILS_FIRST_LINE_COMMENTS. Was the POST-TX sample taken after progression on trastuzumab? If it is unclear, does that change whether these count as acquired resistance?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: You list no pitfall checks. For the two loss samples, compare HER2_IMPACT_LR, FGA and the ERBB2 segment mean in the seg file against the paired PRE-TX sample. Could low purity explain the 'loss', and does the answer change your method?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: Tabulate SITE_OF_TISSUE_BIOPSY / SAMPLE_TYPE for each pre/post pair. Are the two loss events same-lesion comparisons? If they are different-site comparisons, does that change whether they show selection over time?

questions.question: How is 'acquired resistance' to HER2-targeted therapy usually defined in clinical genomics studies (e.g., progression after initial response or stable disease, timing of the post-progression biopsy)?
questions.why: Decides which paired samples are in scope for an acquired-resistance claim, as opposed to any sample taken after treatment.

findings.question: In targeted-panel sequencing of paired pre- and post-treatment tumor biopsies, what criteria are generally used to tell true loss of a focal gene amplification from low tumor purity or sampling of a different lesion?
findings.answer: NOT SETTLED BY THE WEB: the research gateway returned HTTP 403 on every search and contents call, so no page was read. Domain knowledge only: count a loss as true when (1) the post sample has adequate tumor purity, shown by shared truncal alterations (e.g. a TP53 mutation at a similar VAF, or other pre-treatment CNAs) still being present; (2) the ERBB2 log-ratio or segment mean falls to near-diploid instead of only weakening along with the rest of the profile; (3) ideally, loss is confirmed by IHC/FISH or cfDNA. Treat as uninformative any post sample with a flat or low-FGA profile or with missing truncal mutations. Flag samples from a different anatomical site as possible spatial heterogeneity rather than selection.

findings.question: How is 'acquired resistance' to HER2-targeted therapy usually defined in clinical genomics studies (e.g., progression after initial response or stable disease, timing of the post-progression biopsy)?
findings.answer: NOT SETTLED BY THE WEB: the research gateway returned HTTP 403, so no page was read. Domain knowledge only: radiographic (RECIST) progression after an initial objective response or durable stable disease or clinical benefit on HER2-directed therapy, often with a minimum time on therapy (roughly at least 3-6 months). The post-treatment biopsy or cfDNA sample is taken at or after progression, on or soon after the therapy. Progression at first assessment counts as primary resistance. Post-treatment samples without documented prior benefit followed by progression do not count as acquired-resistance samples.
